mbm-2076.clue: I measure a curve with a handful of rice.
mbm-2076.quote: I wanted my quilted kettle to look round. I filled a scrap bag with rice and laid it on the sketch for a shadow. The shadow did all the work my ruler couldn't.

mbm-2077.clue: I know where the hollow sound lives.
mbm-2077.quote: A hold near the climbing gym's top feels like the others but makes a hollow knock under my knuckle. After my first clean ascent I waited at the bottom to hear my partner find it.

mbm-2078.clue: I keep my first bad turn on the fridge.
mbm-2078.quote: I skied a wonderful clean curve followed by a shape like a broken pretzel. My friend photographed our tracks from the lift. I enlarged the pretzel. It has character.

mbm-2079.clue: My train notes have a line for shadows.
mbm-2079.quote: I'm trying to catch the instant a train's shadow crosses the siding before its engine does. In winter the two are a whole platform apart. My best sketch has almost no engine.

mbm-2080.clue: I don't mind a scuffed ball on the practice green.
mbm-2080.quote: At the second-hand shop I picked a golf ball with a blue stripe down one side. Watching that stripe wobble shows me how I hit it. The little ball gives a very honest lesson.

mbm-2081.clue: I start with four glasses by the window.
mbm-2081.quote: Before our son group arrives, I tap the rhythm on the water glasses by the window. By the time the guitar comes in they've each got a little ring of water round the foot.

mbm-2082.clue: My kayak can hold a whole cathedral.
mbm-2082.quote: A tower across the river appears upside down on my polished deck when the sun is low. I paddle to the same bend to find it. One ripple turns the spire into a corkscrew.

mbm-2083.clue: I make souvenirs out of shadows.
mbm-2083.quote: I traced my hand on a postcard beside a famous tower and marked where its shadow ended. Back home the mark is just a pencil dot. I can still picture the whole square.

mbm-2084.clue: The green is three colors if you look long enough.
mbm-2084.quote: I painted a kettle under fluorescent light and hated the flat green. I moved it to the back step and found blue on the lid, lemon on the handle and moss in the dent.

mbm-2085.clue: The little stone has its own towel.
mbm-2085.quote: At the hot spring my father always folds his towel on the same flat stone. One snowy morning it was already wearing a neat white cap. He folded his towel beside it.

mbm-2086.clue: A jump looks smaller when you draw it sideways.
mbm-2086.quote: I sketched the old landing field from memory on the long bus home. Turned sideways, the hedges made an enormous green bird. I colored in the beak and left the compass arrow as its tail.

mbm-2087.clue: The bass line began under a table.
mbm-2087.quote: The café had a wobbly table leg that thumped in time when I rested my elbow on it. I picked up that little pattern on bass. The owner steadied the table and kept the tune.

mbm-2088.clue: I can tell the time by the amber bead.
mbm-2088.quote: I hold my sunglasses with an amber bead on the cord. On a sunny towel the bead drops a small orange spot of light beside my elbow. When it reaches the book, I move under the awning.

mbm-2089.clue: I hide one thing in plain sight.
mbm-2089.quote: I leave a big wooden coin on the table throughout the trick. When the little coin vanishes, a child invariably turns the big one over. That's where I painted the smile.

mbm-2090.clue: My least valuable card came by airmail.
mbm-2090.quote: A friend overseas cut a spare card into a bookmark and tucked it into a letter. I still keep the envelope with its faint round postmark. I built a whole trading deck around that wandering little owl.

mbm-2091.clue: I collect sounds between the signals.
mbm-2091.quote: Turning my ham set one quiet evening I heard the rain barrel, the fridge and a mouse behind the bookcase, all between stations. I drew three tiny marks in the log before my first call.

mbm-2092.clue: That pink square used to miss the bus.
mbm-2092.quote: I quilted my sister's old school skirts into a blanket. One pink hem still has a little chain stitch from the mornings I mended it just as the bus arrived. I left it exactly that short.

mbm-2093.clue: I play the park's shortest grandmaster.
mbm-2093.quote: My opponent's folding stool sank into the muddy grass until only his eyes were level with the board. He kept playing. When he finally stood up he'd won my rook and lost one shoe.

mbm-2094.clue: The handkerchief always lands on the same shoe.
mbm-2094.quote: I practiced the disappearing orange so many times I wore a pale patch in the toe of my slipper catching the silk. My brother watches the slipper now. Smart audience.

mbm-2095.clue: I like the stitches you hardly see.
mbm-2095.quote: My favorite mend is a blue patch inside a blue sleeve. You have to hold it against the window to find my neat little ladder of stitches. I show it to people that way.

mbm-2096.clue: The bow comes before the kettle.
mbm-2096.quote: After martial arts practice my neighbor and I share tea. One morning we bowed to each other in the café before noticing we were holding the same teapot. We poured a very formal cup.

mbm-2097.clue: I leave my thumb in the moon.
mbm-2097.quote: I threw a moon-shaped flask so flat it wanted to roll away. My thumb left a small crater just where the glaze pools. At night that spot is the bluest thing on the shelf.

mbm-2098.clue: We gave the kettle a curtain call.
mbm-2098.quote: The tent was too wet for our usual evening cards. We made shadow puppets with a lantern and the spout of the tea kettle. My daughter's swan had a very convincing whistle.

mbm-2099.clue: I can bowl one quiet frame.
mbm-2099.quote: We played so early the pinsetter was the loudest thing in the building. For one frame the old machine stopped. My ball rolled straight through that unexpected hush and I heard every pin.

mbm-2100.clue: Our commercial breaks have a dress code.
mbm-2100.quote: During the ads Dad throws a blanket over his pajamas and announces the next program in his grandest voice. Mum knotted a bathrobe cord into a bow tie for him. Now he's management.
